article.title: How to Cut In Paint Without Tape
article.summary: Cut in clean paint lines at ceilings and trim without tape: pick the right brush, load it correctly, and use the two-pass method pro painters use.
article.body:
Cutting in means brushing a clean band of paint along ceilings, corners and trim before you roll the wall. With the right brush and a steady two-pass method, you'll get straighter lines than tape gives you, and finish faster.

Steps

  1. Use the right brush and a small pail

    Use a 2 to 2-1/2 in angled sash brush with soft, flagged bristles. Pour about an inch of paint into a small pail you can hold in one hand. Working from the gallon can overloads the brush.

    Done right: you can carry the pail up the ladder and the paint is no deeper than about 1 in.

  2. Load the brush correctly

    Dip only the bottom third of the bristles, then tap both sides against the inside of the pail. Don't wipe it on the rim. The brush should be full but not dripping.

    Done right: you can hold the brush sideways for a few seconds without a drip.

  3. First pass: lay paint away from the line

    Start about 1/2 in below the ceiling or away from the trim. Brush a few strokes to unload paint onto the wall in a band 2 to 3 in wide. This gets paint where you need it without risking the edge.

    Done right: you have a wet band that stops just short of the edge.

  4. Second pass: draw the line

    With the brush now partly unloaded, place the long tip of the angled bristles about 1/8 in from the edge and press lightly so the bristles fan into a fine edge. Pull a long, steady stroke, moving your whole arm, not just your wrist. Let the bristle tips push the paint into the corner.

    Done right: the line is straight and paint meets the edge without touching the ceiling or trim.

  5. Feather the band and keep a wet edge

    Lightly brush out the inner edge of the band so it doesn't leave a ridge. Cut in one wall, then roll it while the cut-in band is still wet, so the two blend without a visible frame.

    Done right: after rolling, you can't see where the brushed band ends.

  6. Fix slips right away

    Wipe a slip off trim or ceiling immediately with a damp rag wrapped around a finger. On a textured ceiling, a quick wipe is better than touch-up paint later.

    Done right: no paint is left on the trim or ceiling once the wall is dry.

Consider a painter if: you have very high ceilings, stairwells or ornate trim. Working safely at height on a ladder or plank needs the right equipment.

FAQ

Is cutting in better than using painter's tape?

With practice, yes. It's faster, and you avoid paint bleeding under the tape or peeling off when you remove it.

What is the best brush for cutting in?

A 2 to 2-1/2 in angled sash brush. Nylon-polyester blends work well with latex paint.

Should I cut in before or after rolling?

Before, one wall at a time, then roll while the cut-in is still wet so the two blend.

How many coats do I cut in?

Cut in for each coat of wall paint, usually two.
